checkpoints.description: [1/1] vectorize the counted array read-modify-write loop with SSE2 so two i64 elements are updated by one paddq, with new documented assembler methods and byte tests, failing-first shape and refusal tests, a paired A/B with identical-binary control, ADR and G-004 diff

impact_assessment.why: the full benchmark on a quiet window still listed array_sum as slower than C and C++ and disassembly showed gcc uses movdqu/paddq to update two elements per iteration while Cairn was scalar
impact_assessment.benefits: array_sum best time fell 8.00 to 7.22 ms (-9.8 percent) and ten-fastest 8.22 to 7.38 ms (-10.2 percent) with identical output
impact_assessment.risks: contract: wrapping i64 sums and byte-identical output; dependency: five new SSE2 emitter methods are part of the x86-64 baseline; concurrency: none; state: no new runtime state
impact_assessment.mitigation: strict match on an even, zero-based, unit-step loop with an invariant addend, refusals for odd bounds and non-invariant addends, byte-level assembler tests, and end-to-end plus IR differential verification

checkpoints.description: [1/1] committed as 1491ebc: five documented SSE2 emitter methods (GPR movq, punpcklqdq, paddq, unaligned indexed movdqu load/store) with byte tests; codegen vectorizes an even, zero-based, unit-step array add loop into a two-lane loop and refuses odd bounds, non-invariant addends and odd entry values; a GPR-source encoding bug was caught by a value check and fixed to 66 REX.W 0F 6E; 1052 end-to-end/IR/codegen/machine tests pass; paired A/B with controls measured -9.8 percent best and -10.2 percent ten-fastest with identical output; ADR-099 and README synced; checklists: passed

checkpoints.description: [1/1] add a deterministic paired-A/B verdict tool to the benchmark harness because two consecutive quiet-window full runs produced contradictory verdicts on byte-identical builds; the tool interleaves Cairn with each baseline and reports an identical-binary control band so 'won' is established against measured noise

impact_assessment.why: the single-run harness verdict flipped between sessions on identical builds, so further speed claims and the all-won condition cannot be arbitrated
impact_assessment.benefits: a reproducible verdict with a measured noise floor
impact_assessment.risks: contract: read-only measurement tool, no compiler change; dependency: reuses the existing harness builders and compilers; concurrency: none; state: writes no benchmark records
impact_assessment.mitigation: unit tests pin the interleaved ratio and control math, and the tool is additive to run_benchmarks.py
